The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.
Summary of Restricted Stock Unit Activity
At the end of 2024, 7,278,000 shares were available to be granted as RSUs, and the following awards, adjusted for the effects of the special
dividend, were outstanding:
• 2,677,000 time-based RSUs, which vest upon continued employment or service over specified periods of time; and
• 122,000 performance-based RSUs, of which 95,000 were granted to executive officers subject to the determination of the attainment of
performance targets for 2024, which occurred in September 2024. At that time, depending upon long-service terms, at least 33% of the
units vested. The remaining awards vest upon continued employment over specified periods of time. Please refer to Note 1 for
accelerated vesting requirements.

Short-Term Borrowings
The Company maintains various short-term bank credit facilities, with a borrowing capacity of $1,198 and $1,234, in 2024 and 2023. Short-term
borrowings outstanding were immaterial at the end of 2024 and 2023.
Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

Our members may utilize their memberships at all of our warehouses and e-commerce sites. Gold Star memberships are available to individuals;
Business memberships are limited to businesses, including individuals with a business license, retail sales license, or comparable document.
Business members may add additional cardholders (affiliates), to which the same annual fee applies. Affiliates are not available for Gold Star
members. During fiscal 2024, our annual fee for these memberships was $60 in the U.S. and varies in other countries. All paid memberships
include a free household card.
Paid members (except affiliates) were eligible to upgrade to an Executive membership in the U.S., for an additional annual fee of $60. Executive
memberships are also available in Canada, Mexico, the U.K., Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Australia, for which the additional fee varies. Executive
members earn a 2% reward on qualified purchases (generally up to a maximum reward of $1,000 per year), redeemable at Costco warehouses.
The sales penetration of Executive members represented approximately 73.3% of worldwide net sales in 2024.
Our member renewal rate was 92.9% in the U.S. and Canada and 90.5% worldwide at the end of 2024. The majority of members renew within
six months following their renewal date. Our renewal rate, which excludes affiliates of Business members, is a trailing calculation that captures
renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as
memberships that have not renewed within the 12 months prior to the reporting date.

Goodwill represents the excess of acquisition cost over the fair value of the net assets acquired and is not subject to amortization. The Company
reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
evaluation is performed at the reporting unit level. If a qualitative assessment indicates that it is more likely than not that the fair value is less
than carrying value, a quantitative analysis is completed using either the income or market approach, or a combination of both. The income
approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies
and transactions to develop metrics to be applied to historical and expected future operating results.

The Company is currently under audit by several jurisdictions in the United States and abroad. Some audits may conclude in the next 12
months, and the unrecognized tax benefits recorded in relation to the audits may differ from actual settlement amounts. It is not practical to
estimate the effect, if any, of any amount of such change during the next 12 months to previously recorded uncertain tax positions in connection

   As per the Consolidated Statements of Income, Operating income is $9,285 million.

2. **Depreciation and Amortization**:  
   From the Cash Flow Statement under "Cash Flows from Operating Activities", depreciation and amortization expenses are given as $2,237 million.

### Adjusted EBITDA Calculation:

\[ \text{Adjusted EBITDA} = \text{Operating Income} + \text{Depreciation and Amortization} \]

\[ \text{Adjusted EBITDA} = \$9,285 \text{ million} + \$2,237 \text{ million} \]

\[ \text{Adjusted EBITDA} = \$11,522 \text{ million} \]

### Conclusion:
The Adjusted EBITDA for Costco Wholesale Corporation for the year ending September 1, 2024, is **$11,522 million**.

Goodwill represents the excess of acquisition cost over the fair value of the net assets acquired and is not subject to amortization. The Company
reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
evaluation is performed at the reporting unit level. If a qualitative assessment indicates that it is more likely than not that the fair value is less
than carrying value, a quantitative analysis is completed using either the income or market approach, or a combination of both. The income

To compute the Adjusted EBITDA Margin for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024, we first need to determine the Adjusted EBITDA figure. The formula for EBITDA is:

\[ \text{EBITDA} = \text{Operating Income} + \text{Depreciation and Amortization} \]

From the provided data:
- Operating income in 2024 is $9,285 million.
- Depreciation and amortization for 2024 can be derived from the statement of cash flows as $2,237 million.

Thus,

\[ \text{EBITDA} = 9,285 + 2,237 = 11,522 \]

Next, we calculate the Adjusted EBITDA Margin by dividing Adjusted EBITDA by Total Revenue:

\[ \text{Adjusted EBITDA Margin} = \frac{\text{EBITDA}}{\text{Total Revenue}} \]

Given that total revenue for 2024 is $254,453 million,

\[ \text{Adjusted EBITDA Margin} = \frac{11,522}{254,453} \approx 0.0453 \]

Expressed as a percentage:

\[ \text{Adjusted EBITDA Margin} \approx 4.53\% \]

So, the Adjusted EBITDA Margin for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately **4.53%**.

To calculate the EV/EBITDA ratio for Costco Wholesale Corporation for the year ending September 1, 2024:

### Step-by-Step Calculation

#### 1. Calculate EBITDA:
EBITDA = Operating Income + Depreciation and Amortization Expenses

From the financial statements:
- **Operating income (OI)** for 2024: $9,285 million
- **Depreciation and amortization** expenses from cash flow statement: $2,237 million

\[ \text{EBITDA} = 9,285 + 2,237 = 11,522 \text{ million dollars} \]

#### 2. Calculate Enterprise Value (EV):
\[ \text{EV} = \text{Market Cap} + \text{Debt} - \text{Cash and Equivalents} \]

From the balance sheet:
- **Total equity**: $23,622 million
- **Long-term debt**: $5,794 million
- **Short-term debt (current portion of long-term debt)**: $103 million
- **Cash and equivalents**: $9,906 million

\[ \text{Market Cap} = \text{Total equity} + \text{(Preferred stock)} - \text{(Additional paid-in capital) + (Accumulated other comprehensive loss)} \]
Since there are no preferred shares issued:
\[ \text{Market Cap} = 23,622 + 0 - 1,828 = 21,794 \]

Total Debt:
- Long-term debt: $5,794 million
- Current portion of long-term debt (short-term): $103 million

\[ \text{Debt} = 5,794 + 103 = 5,897 \text{ million dollars} \]

Enterprise Value:
\[ \text{EV} = 21,794 + 5,897 - 9,906 = 17,785 \text{ million dollars} \]

#### 3. Calculate EV/EBITDA Ratio:

\[ \text{EV/EBITDA} = \frac{\text{Enterprise Value (EV)}}{\text{EBITDA}} \]
\[ \text{EV/EBITDA} = \frac{17,785}{11,522} \approx 1.54 \]

### Conclusion:
The EV/EBITDA ratio for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024 is approximately **1.54**.

To calculate the Enterprise Value (EV) for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024, we need to follow these steps:

### Step 1: Market Value of Equity

First, let’s determine the market value of equity. This is calculated by multiplying the diluted shares outstanding by the current stock price.

- **Diluted Shares Outstanding (September 1, 2024)**: 444,759,000
- **Costco Stock Price**: $940

\[ \text{Market Value of Equity} = 444,759,000 \times \$940 = \$418,362,860,000 \]

### Step 2: Total Debt (Including Current Portion)

Next, we need to sum up the total debt from both short-term and long-term liabilities.

- **Long-Term Debt**: $5,794 million
- **Current Portion of Long-Term Debt**: $103 million

\[ \text{Total Debt} = \$5,794M + \$103M = \$5,897M \]

### Step 3: Cash and Short-term Investments (Excess Cash)

We need to subtract the excess cash from our total debt as per the instructions.

- **Cash and Cash Equivalents**: $9,906 million
- **Short-Term Investments**: $1,238 million

\[ \text{Excess Cash} = \$9,906M + \$1,238M = \$11,144M \]

### Step 4: Enterprise Value Calculation

Finally, we can calculate the enterprise value using the formula:

\[ \text{Enterprise Value (EV)} = \text{Market Value of Equity} + \text{Total Debt} - \text{Excess Cash} \]

Plugging in our values:

\[ \text{EV} = \$418,362,860,000 + \$5,897M - \$11,144M \]
\[ \text{EV} = \$418,362,860,000 + \$5,897,000,000 - \$11,144,000,000 \]
\[ \text{EV} = \$412,115,860,000 \]

### Final Answer:

The Enterprise Value (EV) for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024 is **$412.1 billion**.

To calculate the Equity Value of Costco Wholesale Corporation for 2024, we use the relationship between Enterprise Value (EV), Debt, Cash & Equivalents, and Equity:

\[ \text{Equity Value} = \text{Enterprise Value} - (\text{Debt} - \text{Cash}) \]

Given:
- **Enterprise Value** for 2024 is $420 billion.
- The only non-operating asset not factored into Enterprise Value is excess cash, which is given as $9,906 million (or $9.906 billion).

From the Balance Sheet data provided:
- Long-term debt excluding current portion = $5,794 million ($5.794 billion).
- Current liabilities include a current portion of long-term debt = $103 million.
- Total Debt = $5,897 million ($5.794 + $0.103) or $5.897 billion.

Now we can plug in the values into the formula:

\[ \text{Equity Value} = 420 - (5.897 - 9.906) = 420 - (-4.009) = 420 + 4.009 = 424.009 \]

Therefore, the Equity Value in 2024 is approximately **$424.01 billion**.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

To calculate the Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) for Costco Wholesale Corporation for 2024, we need to consider both the cost of equity and the cost of debt. The formula for WACC is:

\[ \text{WACC} = w_d \times r_d \times (1 - t_c) + w_e \times r_e \]

Where:
- \(w_d\) = weight of debt
- \(r_d\) = cost of debt
- \(t_c\) = corporate tax rate
- \(w_e\) = weight of equity
- \(r_e\) = cost of equity

### Step 1: Cost of Debt (\( r_d \))
The given cost of debt is 6%.

### Step 2: Corporate Tax Rate (\( t_c \))
From the income statement, we see that the company's provision for income taxes in 2024 was $2,373 million on income before income tax of $9,740 million. The effective tax rate can be calculated as:
\[ \text{Effective Tax Rate} = \frac{\text{Provision for Income Taxes}}{\text{Income Before Income Taxes}} = \frac{2,373}{9,740} \approx 24.35\% \]

### Step 3: Cost of Equity (\( r_e \))
We can use the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) to estimate the cost of equity:
\[ r_e = R_f + \beta \times (R_m - R_f) \]
Where:
- \( R_f \) is the risk-free rate
- \( \beta \) is the beta coefficient
- \( R_m \) is the market return

Given:
- Risk-Free Rate (\( R_f \)) = 10Y Treasury Yield = 4.617%
- Beta (\( \beta \)) = 0.79
- Market Return (\( R_m \)) = 11%

\[ r_e = 4.617\% + 0.79 \times (11\% - 4.617\%) \]
\[ r_e = 4.617\% + 0.79 \times 6.383\% \]
\[ r_e = 4.617\% + 5.042\% \]
\[ r_e = 9.659\% \]

### Step 4: Weights of Debt and Equity (\( w_d \) and \( w_e \))
To find the weights, we need total debt and total equity from the balance sheet.

Total Debt:
- Long-term debt (excluding current portion): $5,794 million
- Current portion of long-term debt: $103 million

\[ \text{Total Debt} = 5,794 + 103 = 5,897 \text{ million dollars} \]

Total Equity:
- Common stock (par value): $2 million
- Additional paid-in capital: $7,829 million
- Retained earnings: $17,619 million

\[ \text{Total Equity} = 2 + 7,829 + 17,619 = 25,440 \text{ million dollars} \]

Market Value of Debt is generally assumed to be the book value unless specified otherwise.

### Step 5: Calculate WACC
First, calculate the weights:
\[ w_d = \frac{\text{Total Debt}}{\text{Total Debt} + \text{Total Equity}} = \frac{5,897}{5,897 + 25,440} = \frac{5,897}{31,337} \approx 0.1881 \]
\[ w_e = \frac{\text{Total Equity}}{\text{Total Debt} + \text{Total Equity}} = \frac{25,440}{5,897 + 25,440} = \frac{25,440}{31,337} \approx 0.8119 \]

Now, plug into the WACC formula:
\[ \text{WACC} = w_d \times r_d \times (1 - t_c) + w_e \times r_e \]
\[ \text{WACC} = 0.1881 \times 6\% \times (1 - 24.35\%) + 0.8119 \times 9.659\% \]
\[ \text{WACC} = 0.1881 \times 0.06 \times 0.7565 + 0.8119 \times 0.09659 \]
\[ \text{WACC} = 0.00842 + 0.07837 \approx 0.08679 \]

Therefore, the WACC for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately **8.68%**.

The market debt-to-equity ratio is a financial metric that reflects the proportion of a company's equity to its total debt, based on the current market values of those components. It is calculated as follows:

\[ \text{Market Debt-to-Equity Ratio} = \frac{\text{Total Market Value of Debt}}{\text{Total Market Value of Equity}} \]

To calculate this for Costco Wholesale Corporation using available data and assumptions:

1. **Total Market Value of Debt**: This would typically include the market value of all outstanding debt, such as bonds or other borrowings. Since specific market values are not provided in the context, we use the book value of long-term debt as an approximation:
   - Long-term debt (excluding current portion) = $5,794 million

2. **Total Market Value of Equity**: This is usually calculated using the number of shares outstanding and the stock price.
   - Shares Outstanding: 443,126,000
   - Stock Price: $940 per share
   
   \[ \text{Market Value of Equity} = 443,126,000 \times \$940 = \$417,805,040,000 \]

Now we can calculate the market debt-to-equity ratio:

\[ \text{Market Debt-to-Equity Ratio} = \frac{\$5,794,000,000}{\$417,805,040,000} \approx 0.0139 \]

To express this as a ratio:

\[ \text{Market Debt-to-Equity Ratio} = 0.0139 : 1 \]

This indicates that for every dollar of equity, Costco has approximately $0.0139 in debt based on market values.

In summary, the market debt-to-equity ratio for Costco Wholesale Corporation is approximately **0.014** or **1:70** (rounded to simplify interpretation). This suggests a relatively low level of financial leverage compared to equity funding.

Expressed as a percentage, this is approximately **66.2%**.

So, the Debt to Value ratio for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is **66.2%**.

To calculate the Equity to Value ratio for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024:

1. **Identify Total Equity from the Balance Sheet:**
   - Total Equity on September 1, 2024 = $23,622 million

2. **Determine the Market Capitalization (Value):**
   - To find market capitalization, multiply the number of shares by the stock price.
   - Number of Shares Outstanding as of September 1, 2024: 443,126,000
   - Stock Price on September 1, 2024: $940

\[ \text{Market Capitalization} = \text{Number of Shares} \times \text{Stock Price} \]
\[ \text{Market Capitalization} = 443,126,000 \times 940 = 417,582,040,000 \]

3. **Calculate Equity to Value Ratio:**
   - Equity to Value ratio is calculated as:
\[ \text{Equity to Value} = \frac{\text{Total Equity}}{\text{Market Capitalization}} \]
\[ \text{Equity to Value} = \frac{23,622}{417,582.04} = 0.0565 \]

Therefore, the Equity to Value ratio for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024 is approximately **0.0565** or **5.65%**.

To determine the statutory/marginal tax rates on adjusted EBIT for Costco Wholesale Corporation, we need to look at how their income taxes are calculated based on the provided financial statements.

From the **Income Taxes** section of Costco's Consolidated Statements:

1. **Income Before Income Taxes**: 
   - 2024: $9,740 million
   - 2023: $8,487 million

2. **Provision for Income Taxes**:
   - 2024: $2,373 million
   - 2023: $2,195 million
   
To calculate the effective tax rate (which approximates the marginal tax rate):

\[
\text{Effective Tax Rate} = \left( \frac{\text{Provision for Income Taxes}}{\text{Income Before Income Taxes}} \right) \times 100
\]

For **2024**:
\[
\text{Effective Tax Rate} = \left( \frac{2,373}{9,740} \right) \times 100 \approx 24.36\%
\]

For **2023**:
\[
\text{Effective Tax Rate} = \left( \frac{2,195}{8,487} \right) \times 100 \approx 25.86\%
\]

The statutory federal tax rate is typically 21% as per the corporate income tax rates in the U.S., but this does not account for state taxes and other factors that contribute to the overall effective tax rate.

Given these figures, Costco's effective (marginal) tax rate has been around 24-25%. For a precise calculation of the statutory/marginal tax on Adjusted EBIT, you would need more granular information such as specific state taxes and foreign taxes. However, based on the given data, we can infer that Costco’s marginal tax rate is approximately **24.36%** in 2024.

### Summary:
- The statutory federal corporate income tax rate for U.S. companies is generally around 21%, but effective rates account for additional factors like state taxes and foreign operations.
- For Costco Wholesale Corporation, the effective (marginal) tax rate is approximately **24.36%** in 2024.

For a more detailed breakdown of state-specific and international impacts, you would need to refer to the company's specific disclosures or consult their annual report for additional details on jurisdictional tax rates and provisions.

increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.

and transactions to develop metrics to be applied to historical and expected future operating results.

The operating cash tax rate for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 can be calculated based on the income before income taxes and the provision for income taxes provided in the financial statements.

From the Consolidated Statements of Income:
- Income before income taxes: $9,740 million
- Provision for income taxes: $2,373 million

The operating cash tax rate is computed as follows:

\[ \text{Operating Cash Tax Rate} = \left( \frac{\text{Provision for Income Taxes}}{\text{Income Before Income Taxes}} \right) \times 100 \]

Substituting the values from the financial statements:

\[ \text{Operating Cash Tax Rate} = \left( \frac{2,373}{9,740} \right) \times 100 \approx 24.35\% \]

Therefore, the operating cash tax rate for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately **24.4%**.

To calculate the unlevered beta for Costco Wholesale Corporation for 2024, we need to use the formula:

\[ \beta_{\text{unlevered}} = \frac{\beta_{\text{equity}}}{1 + (1 - T) \left( \frac{D}{E} \right)} \]

Where:
- \( \beta_{\text{equity}} \) is the levered beta of Costco's equity.
- \( T \) is the corporate tax rate.
- \( D \) is the total debt.
- \( E \) is the market value of equity.

Given data:
- Levered Beta (\( \beta_{\text{equity}} \)) = 0.79
- Cost of Debt (Assume this implies an effective interest rate on debt) = 6%
- Corporate Tax Rate (\( T \)) = 1 - (Cost of Treasury Bond Yield / Market Return) = 1 - (4.617% / 11%) ≈ 0.58
- Total Debt (\( D \)) from the balance sheet as of September 1, 2024: $5,794 million
- Market Value of Equity (\( E \)): \( \text{Number of shares} \times \text{Stock Price} = 443,126,000 \times \$940 ≈ \$418,089.04 \) billion

Now calculate the debt-to-equity ratio:

\[ D/E = \frac{5794}{418089.04} \approx 0.0139 \]

Next, apply this to the formula for unlevered beta:

\[ \beta_{\text{unlevered}} = \frac{0.79}{1 + (1 - 0.58) \times 0.0139} \]
\[ \beta_{\text{unlevered}} = \frac{0.79}{1 + 0.42 \times 0.0139} \]
\[ \beta_{\text{unlevered}} = \frac{0.79}{1 + 0.005818} \]
\[ \beta_{\text{unlevered}} = \frac{0.79}{1.005818} \approx 0.786 \]

Therefore, the unlevered beta for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024, is approximately **0.786**.

To compute the Debt for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024, including debt equivalents like lease liabilities, follow these steps:

### Step-by-Step Calculation

1. **Long-Term Debt**:
   - From the balance sheet, long-term debt excluding current portion is given as $5,794 million.

2. **Operating Lease Liabilities**:
   - Operating lease liabilities are included in other long-term liabilities and are reported at $2,375 million.

3. **Finance Lease Liabilities**:
   - Finance lease liabilities are also part of other long-term liabilities and total $1,351 million.

### Total Debt Calculation

- **Long-Term Debt**: $5,794 million
- **Operating Lease Liabilities (Debt Equivalent)**: $2,375 million
- **Finance Lease Liabilities (Debt Equivalent)**: $1,351 million

Total Debt = Long-Term Debt + Operating Lease Liabilities + Finance Lease Liabilities  
= $5,794 million + $2,375 million + $1,351 million  
= $9,520 million

### Conclusion
The total debt for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024, including debt equivalents such as lease liabilities, is **$9.52 billion**.

To calculate the Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024, we need to use the following formula:

\[ \text{ROIC} = \frac{\text{Net Operating Profit After Taxes (NOPAT)}}{\text{Invested Capital}} \]

### Step 1: Calculate NOPAT
NOPAT is calculated as follows:
\[ \text{NOPAT} = \text{Operating Income} - \text{Taxes on Operating Income} \]
From the financial statements, we have:
- **Operating Income for 2024**: $9,285 million
- **Income Before Income Taxes for 2024**: $9,740 million
- **Provision for Income Taxes for 2024**: $2,373 million

Since the provision for income taxes is given and includes both federal and state taxes, we can use it directly to calculate NOPAT:
\[ \text{NOPAT} = \$9,285 - \$2,373 = \$6,912 \text{ million} \]

### Step 2: Calculate Invested Capital
Invested capital is the sum of total debt and shareholders' equity minus cash and cash equivalents. The formula is:
\[ \text{Invested Capital} = \text{Total Debt} + \text{Shareholders' Equity} - \text{Cash and Cash Equivalents} \]

From the financial statements, we have:
- **Long-term debt**: $5,794 million
- **Current portion of long-term debt**: $103 million
- **Total liabilities excluding current portion of long-term debt**: $46,209 - 5,794 = $40,415 million (but we don't need this as we have the total debt)
- **Shareholders' equity**: $23,622 million
- **Cash and cash equivalents**: $9,906 million

So,
\[ \text{Invested Capital} = \$5,794 + \$23,622 - \$9,906 = \$19,510 \text{ million} \]

### Step 3: Calculate ROIC
Now we can calculate the ROIC:
\[ \text{ROIC} = \frac{\$6,912}{\$19,510} \approx 0.3547 \]
Expressed as a percentage,
\[ \text{ROIC} \approx 35.47\% \]

So, the ROIC for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately **35.47%**.

To determine the Invested Capital including Goodwill for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024, we need to follow these steps:

### Step-by-Step Calculation

#### 1. **Determine Operating Cash (Maximum Potential)**
The context suggests using 2% of revenue as max potential operating cash.

\[
\text{Operating Cash} = 2\% \times \text{Total Revenue}
\]

For the year ending September 1, 2024:
\[
\text{Total Revenue} = \$254,453 \text{ million}
\]
\[
\text{Operating Cash} = 0.02 \times 254,453 = \$5,089.06 \text{ million}
\]

#### 2. **Identify Total Debt**
From the balance sheet:

- Long-term debt (excluding current portion): $5,794 million
- Current liabilities: $35,464 million

For simplicity, we assume all current liabilities are not part of invested capital unless specified otherwise.

\[
\text{Total Debt} = \text{Long-term debt} = \$5,794 \text{ million}
\]

#### 3. **Identify Shareholders' Equity**
From the balance sheet:

- Total equity: $23,622 million

This includes:
- Preferred stock (no shares issued and outstanding): $0
- Common stock ($0.005 par value; 443,126,000 shares issued and outstanding): $2 million
- Additional paid-in capital: $7,829 million
- Accumulated other comprehensive loss: $(1,828) million
- Retained earnings: $17,619 million

#### 4. **Calculate Invested Capital (Debt + Equity - Cash)**
\[
\text{Invested Capital} = \text{Total Debt} + \text{Total Equity} - \text{Operating Cash}
\]

Given:
- Operating cash: $5,089.06 million

\[
\text{Invested Capital} = 5,794 + 23,622 - 5,089.06 = \$24,326.94 \text{ million}
\]

#### 5. **Include Goodwill**
Goodwill is listed under other long-term assets:

- Goodwill: $994 million

Add this to the Invested Capital calculated above.

\[
\text{Invested Capital including Goodwill} = \$24,326.94 + \$994 = \$25,320.94 \text{ million}
\]

### Final Answer
The Invested Capital for Costco Wholesale Corporation including Goodwill as of September 1, 2024 is **$25,320.94 million**.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

To determine the Invested Capital excluding Goodwill for Costco Wholesale Corporation for 2024:

1. **Equity**: From the consolidated balance sheet, equity is:
   - Additional paid-in capital: $7,829 million
   - Retained earnings: $17,619 million
   - Total Equity: $23,622 million

2. **Goodwill**: Goodwill is included in other long-term assets and is reported as $953 million (United States) + $26 million (Canada) + $15 million (Other International) = $1,004 million.

3. **Debt**:
   - Long-term debt excluding current portion: $5,794 million
   - Current liabilities include deferred membership fees of $2,501 million which is a liability related to future revenue.
   
   Total Debt (including current liabilities relevant for invested capital calculation): $5,794 + $2,501 = $8,295 million

4. **Net Working Capital**:
   - Current assets: $34,246 million
   - Current liabilities: $35,464 million
   
   Net working capital is negative: $(35,464 - 34,246) = $(1,218) million

To calculate Invested Capital:
\[ \text{Invested Capital} = \text{Equity} + \text{Debt} - \text{Net Working Capital} \]
\[ \text{Invested Capital excluding Goodwill} = 23,622 + 8,295 - (1,218) - 1,004 \]
\[ \text{Invested Capital excluding Goodwill} = 23,622 + 8,295 - 1,218 - 1,004 \]
\[ \text{Invested Capital excluding Goodwill} = 29,705 \]

To determine the maximum potential operating cash using 2% of revenue:
\[ \text{Revenue for 2024} = \$254,453 million \]
\[ \text{Maximum Potential Operating Cash} = 2\% \times 254,453 = 0.02 \times 254,453 = 5,089 \text{ million dollars} \]

So the Invested Capital excluding Goodwill for Costco in 2024 is $29,705 million and the maximum potential operating cash is $5,089 million.

To determine Invested Capital including Goodwill for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 3, 2023, we need to calculate the sum of Total Assets minus Non-interest bearing Current Liabilities and Other Long-term Liabilities (excluding goodwill), then add back Goodwill. The formula can be expressed as:

\[ \text{Invested Capital} = \text{Total Assets} - (\text{Non-Interest Bearing Current Liabilities} + \text{Other Long-Term Liabilities}) + \text{Goodwill} \]

### Step-by-step Calculation

1. **Identify Total Assets:**
   From the balance sheet as of September 3, 2023:
   - Total Assets = $68,994 million

2. **Identify Non-Interest Bearing Current Liabilities and Other Long-Term Liabilities:**
   - Non-interest bearing current liabilities include Accounts payable ($17,483M), Accrued salaries and benefits ($4,278M), Accrued member rewards ($2,150M), Deferred membership fees ($2,337M).
   - Other long-term liabilities = $2,550 million
   - Current portion of Long-Term Debt is considered interest-bearing and not included in non-interest bearing current liabilities.

3. **Calculate Non-Interest Bearing Liabilities:**
   \[ \text{Non-interest Bearing Current Liabilities} = 17,483 + 4,278 + 2,150 + 2,337 = 26,248 \]
   
4. **Add Other Long-Term Liabilities (excluding goodwill):**
   - Total non-interest bearing liabilities: \(26,248 + 2,550 = 28,798\) million

5. **Identify Goodwill:**
   From the balance sheet:
   - Goodwill is included in other long-term assets and amounts to $15M as of September 3, 2023.

6. **Calculate Invested Capital:**
   \[ \text{Invested Capital} = 68,994 - 28,798 + 15 = 40,211 \]

### Maximum Operating Cash
The provided context suggests using up to 2% of revenue as the maximum potential operating cash. For Costco in 2023:

\[ \text{Max Potential Operating Cash} = 0.02 \times 242,290 = 4,845.8 \]

### Final Calculation
The Invested Capital including Goodwill for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 3, 2023 is:
\[ \boxed{40,211 \text{ million dollars}} \]

To determine the Average Invested Capital (AIC) including Goodwill for Costco Wholesale Corporation over the years 2023 and 2024, we need to follow these steps:

1. **Identify Total Assets**: This includes all assets listed on the balance sheet.

2. **Identify Total Liabilities**: This includes current liabilities and long-term liabilities.

3. **Calculate Equity**: Subtract total liabilities from total assets to get equity. The equity section also includes goodwill under other long-term assets.

4. **Include Goodwill in Invested Capital Calculation**:
   - From the balance sheet, note that goodwill is listed as $994 million (Total of United States: $953 million, Canada: $26 million, and Other International: $15 million).

5. **Calculate Total Invested Capital for Each Year**: 
    \[
    \text{Invested Capital} = \text{Total Assets} - \text{Non-interest-bearing Liabilities}
    \]
   Since there is no specific mention of non-interest-bearing liabilities, we consider the equity plus goodwill as invested capital.

### For 2023:
- **Total Assets**: $68,994 million
- **Total Liabilities**: $43,936 million
- **Equity (including accumulated other comprehensive loss)**: $25,058 million

Invested Capital for 2023 including Goodwill:
\[
\text{Invested Capital}_{2023} = \text{Total Assets}_{2023} + \text{Goodwill}
= 68,994 + 994
= 69,988 \text{ million dollars}
\]

### For 2024:
- **Total Assets**: $69,831 million
- **Total Liabilities**: $46,209 million
- **Equity (including accumulated other comprehensive loss)**: $23,622 million

Invested Capital for 2024 including Goodwill:
\[
\text{Invested Capital}_{2024} = \text{Total Assets}_{2024} + \text{Goodwill}
= 69,831 + 994
= 70,825 \text{ million dollars}
\]

### Average Invested Capital:
To find the average invested capital over 2023 and 2024:
\[
\text{Average Invested Capital} = \frac{\text{Invested Capital}_{2023} + \text{Invested Capital}_{2024}}{2}
= \frac{69,988 + 70,825}{2}
= \frac{140,813}{2}
= 70,406.5 \text{ million dollars}
\]

Thus, the Average Invested Capital including Goodwill for Costco Wholesale Corporation over 2023 and 2024 is **$70,406.5 million**.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

To find the operating portion of long-term assets and net long-term liabilities for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2023:

1. **Operating Lease Right-of-Use Assets**: From the balance sheet, this is $2,713 million.

2. **Finance Lease Assets (if any)**: There are no finance lease assets listed separately under operating portion of long-term assets but it's included under total lease assets as 1,325 million.

However, since we're specifically asked for the "operating portion" and the context provided indicates that operating leases should be prioritized over finance leases, we focus on the Operating Lease Right-of-Use Assets which is $2,713 million.

3. **Current Portion of Long-Term Debt**: This is included under current liabilities as $1,081 million in 2023.

4. **Total Long-term Liabilities (excluding current portion)**: From the balance sheet, this includes:
   - Long-term debt excluding current portion: $5,377 million
   - Operating lease liabilities excluding current portion: $2,291 million ($2,426 total less $135 current)
   
The **operating portion of long-term assets** would be the operating lease right-of-use assets:
\[ \text{Operating Lease Right-of-Use Assets} = 2,713 \text{ million dollars} \]

The **net long-term liabilities** (excluding the current portion) can be calculated as follows:

\[ \text{Net Long-Term Liabilities} = (\text{Total Long-Term Debt excluding Current Portion}) + (\text{Operating Lease Liabilities excluding Current Portion}) - (\text{Other Long-Term Assets}) \]
\[ \text{Net Long-Term Liabilities} = 5,377 + 2,291 - (3,718) = 3,950 \text{ million dollars} \]

So:
- **Operating portion of long-term assets** is $2,713 million.
- **Net long-term liabilities** is $3,950 million.

To determine the change in the operating portion of long-term assets (operating lease right-of-use assets) and net long-term liabilities from 2023 to 2024:

1. **Operating Lease Right-Of-Use Assets:**
   - 2024: $2,617 million
   - 2023: $2,713 million

The change in operating lease right-of-use assets from 2023 to 2024 is:
\[ \text{Change} = \$2,617\text{ million} - \$2,713\text{ million} = -\$96\text{ million} \]

2. **Net Long-Term Liabilities:**
   The net long-term liabilities include both operating lease and finance lease liabilities minus any assets.

   - **Operating Lease Liabilities (Current + Non-Current):** 
     - 2024: $2,375 million
     - 2023: $2,426 million

   - **Finance Lease Liabilities (Current + Non-Current):**
     - 2024: $1,351 million
     - 2023: $1,303 million

The total long-term liabilities are:
\[ \text{Total Long-Term Liabilities} = \$2,375\text{ million} + \$1,351\text{ million} = \$3,726\text{ million (2024)} \]
\[ \text{Total Long-Term Liabilities} = \$2,426\text{ million} + \$1,303\text{ million} = \$3,729\text{ million (2023)} \]

Since there are no specific long-term lease assets provided in the context other than operating lease right-of-use assets ($2,617 million for 2024 and $2,713 million for 2023), we will consider only these for net long-term liabilities:

\[ \text{Net Long-Term Liabilities (Approximate)} = \$3,726\text{ million} - \$2,617\text{ million} = \$1,109\text{ million (2024)} \]
\[ \text{Net Long-Term Liabilities (Approximate)} = \$3,729\text{ million} - \$2,713\text{ million} = \$1,016\text{ million (2023)} \]

The change in net long-term liabilities from 2023 to 2024:
\[ \text{Change} = \$1,109\text{ million} - \$1,016\text{ million} = +\$93\text{ million} \]

Therefore, the changes are as follows:
- **Operating Lease Right-of-Use Assets:** Decreased by $96 million.
- **Net Long-Term Liabilities (Approximate):** Increased by $93 million.

To determine the portion of other long-term assets that's not accounted for in 2024, net of the portion of other long-term operating liabilities not accounted for:

1. Identify "Other long-term assets" from the balance sheet: 
   - 2024: $3,936 million
   - 2023: $3,718 million

2. Identify "Operating lease right-of-use assets," which are included in other long-term assets:
   - This is given as $2,617 million for 2024.

3. Subtract operating lease right-of-use assets from other long-term assets to get the portion of other long-term assets not accounted for by operating leases:
   - For 2024: $3,936 million - $2,617 million = $1,319 million

4. Identify "Long-term operating lease liabilities," which are included in other long-term liabilities:
   - This is given as $2,375 million for 2024.

Since the question asks specifically about the portion not accounted for:

The calculation is essentially:
- Other long-term assets ($1,319 million) minus Long-term operating lease liabilities ($2,375 million).

However, since other long-term liabilities include both finance and operating leases, but we are only looking at the difference between non-operating lease components within these categories:

Since there's no direct overlap given (other than operating leases), effectively:
- Non-operating lease portion of other long-term assets: $1,319 million.
- Long-term operating lease liabilities: $2,375 million (but we're considering only the non-overlapping part).

Thus, for net difference specifically asked:

\[ \text{Net Difference} = \$1,319 \text{ million} - (\$2,375 \text{ million} - Operating Lease Components) \]

Since operating lease components are already accounted for:
\[ \text{Net Difference} = \$1,319 \text{ million} - \$0 (non-overlapping liabilities) \]

So the net difference is simply:

\[ \$1,319 \text{ million} \]

To measure the change between 2023 and 2024 for the operating metric after separating other long-term assets (net of long-term liabilities), follow these steps:

1. **Identify Other Long-Term Assets and Liabilities:**
   - As of September 1, 2024: Other long-term assets = $3,936 million
   - As of September 3, 2023: Other long-term assets = $3,718 million

2. **Identify Long-Term Liabilities in the Same Line Item:**
   - These are included under "Other long-term liabilities" and for both years:
     - As of September 1, 2024: Other long-term liabilities = $2,576 million
     - As of September 3, 2023: Other long-term liabilities = $2,550 million

3. **Calculate the Net Value (Other Long-Term Assets Minus Other Long-Term Liabilities):**
   - For 2024:
     \[
     \text{Net value} = \$3,936\text{M} - \$2,576\text{M} = \$1,360\text{M}
     \]
   - For 2023:
     \[
     \text{Net value} = \$3,718\text{M} - \$2,550\text{M} = \$1,168\text{M}
     \]

4. **Determine the Change:**
   - Calculate the difference between 2024 and 2023:
     \[
     \Delta (\text{Net value}) = \$1,360\text{M} - \$1,168\text{M} = \$192\text{M}
     \]

Therefore, the change in this operating metric from 2023 to 2024 is an increase of $192 million.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as
memberships that have not renewed within the 12 months prior to the reporting date.

Goodwill represents the excess of acquisition cost over the fair value of the net assets acquired and is not subject to amortization. The Company
reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
evaluation is performed at the reporting unit level. If a qualitative assessment indicates that it is more likely than not that the fair value is less
than carrying value, a quantitative analysis is completed using either the income or market approach, or a combination of both. The income
approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies
and transactions to develop metrics to be applied to historical and expected future operating results.

To calculate Net Operating Profit After Tax (NOPAT) for Costco Wholesale Corporation for the year ending September 1, 2024, we need to adjust the income before taxes and remove non-operating items such as interest expense. Here's a step-by-step breakdown:

### Income Before Taxes:
From the provided financial statements:
\[ \text{Income Before Income Taxes} = \$9,740 \]

### Interest Expense Adjustment:
We need to add back the interest expense since NOPAT excludes financing costs.
\[ \text{Interest Expense} = -\$169 \]
\[ \text{NOPAT (before tax adjustments)} = \$9,740 + (-\$169) = \$9,571 \]

### Income Tax Adjustment:
We need to adjust for income taxes. We will use the tax provision from the financial statements.

From the provided data:
\[ \text{Provision for Income Taxes} = \$2,373 \]

Thus,
\[ \text{NOPAT (after tax)} = (\$9,571 - \$2,373) = \$7,198 \]

### Conclusion
The NOPAT for Costco Wholesale Corporation for the year ending September 1, 2024 is:
\[ \boxed{\$7,198} \]

To estimate the variable lease assets for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2023:

From the provided balance sheets:
- Operating lease right-of-use assets as of September 3, 2023: $2,713 million

According to Note 5—Leases, there are no specific details given about separating fixed and variable components within operating lease assets. However, since we need an estimate for the variable component in 2023:

- Total operating lease costs (including both fixed and variable) as of September 3, 2023: $692 million
- Variable lease costs specifically mentioned for 2023: $160 million

Given that the total lease costs are reported but not broken down into fixed versus variable parts in the balance sheet context provided, we can infer a portion of the operating lease right-of-use assets relate to variable components based on the proportion of variable costs out of total costs:

\[
\text{Proportion of Variable Costs} = \frac{\text{Variable Lease Costs}}{\text{Total Operating Lease Costs}} = \frac{160}{692}
\]

Calculating this proportion:
\[
\approx 0.231
\]

Therefore, an estimate for the variable lease assets out of total operating lease right-of-use assets would be:

\[
\text{Variable Lease Assets} = 2,713 \times 0.231 \approx 625.9 \text{ million dollars}
\]

So, the estimated value of variable lease assets in 2023 is approximately $625.9 million.

To estimate the change in variable lease assets from 2023 to 2024 for Costco Wholesale Corporation:

1. **Identify Variable Lease Assets**: From the context provided, it appears that operating lease right-of-use (ROU) assets represent variable lease assets.

2. **Values from Financial Statements**:
   - Operating ROU assets at September 3, 2023: $2,713 million
   - Operating ROU assets at September 1, 2024: $2,617 million

3. **Calculate the Change**:
   \[
   \text{Change} = \text{Value in 2024} - \text{Value in 2023}
   \]
   \[
   \text{Change} = \$2,617\,\text{million} - \$2,713\,\text{million} = -\$96\,\text{million}
   \]

Therefore, the change in variable lease assets from 2023 to 2024 is a decrease of $96 million.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.

To calculate the Operating Working Capital (OWC) for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024, using the provided financial data:

**Operating Working Capital = Current Assets - Current Liabilities + Max Potential Operating Cash**

Given:
- **Current Assets**: $34,246 million
- **Current Liabilities**: $35,464 million

Next, we need to determine the "Max Potential Operating Cash" which is given as 2% of revenue. For Costco Wholesale Corporation:

**Revenue (Net Sales) for 2024:** $249,625 million
- **Max Potential Operating Cash**: \( 2\% \times \$249,625 = 0.02 \times 249,625 = \$4,992.5 \) million

Now we can calculate the OWC:

\[ \text{OWC} = \$34,246 - \$35,464 + \$4,992.5 \]

\[ \text{OWC} = -\$1,218 + \$4,992.5 \]

\[ \text{OWC} = \$3,774.5 \] million

So, the Operating Working Capital for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024 is **$3,774.5 million**.

Goodwill represents the excess of acquisition cost over the fair value of the net assets acquired and is not subject to amortization. The Company
reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
evaluation is performed at the reporting unit level. If a qualitative assessment indicates that it is more likely than not that the fair value is less
than carrying value, a quantitative analysis is completed using either the income or market approach, or a combination of both. The income

To calculate the EBIT Interest Coverage Ratio for Costco Wholesale Corporation for 2024, we need to determine both the earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) and the total interest expense.

### Step-by-Step Calculation:

1. **Earnings Before Interest and Taxes (EBIT):**
   - Operating income for 2024 is given as $9,285 million.
   - Add back interest expense to get EBIT since operating income already includes non-operating items like interest expense.
   
   \[
   \text{EBIT} = \text{Operating Income} + \text{Interest Expense}
   \]
   
   \[
   \text{EBIT} = 9,285 + 169 = 9,454 \text{ million dollars}
   \]

2. **Total Interest Expense:**
   - The interest expense for 2024 is given as $169 million.

3. **Interest Coverage Ratio Calculation:**

\[
\text{EBIT Interest Coverage Ratio} = \frac{\text{EBIT}}{\text{Interest Expense}}
\]

\[
\text{EBIT Interest Coverage Ratio} = \frac{9,454}{169} \approx 56.03
\]

### Conclusion:
The EBIT Interest Coverage Ratio for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately **56.03** times.

To calculate the EBITA Interest Coverage Ratio for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024, we need to follow these steps:

1. **Calculate EBITA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, and Amortization):**
   - Start with Operating Income: $9,285 million.
   - Add back Depreciation and amortization expense: $2,237 million (from the cash flow statement).

   \[
   \text{EBITA} = \$9,285 + \$2,237 = \$11,522 \text{ million}
   \]

2. **Identify Interest Expense:**
   - From the income statement, Interest expense is $(169) million.

3. **Calculate EBITA Interest Coverage Ratio:**
   The formula for the EBITA interest coverage ratio is:

   \[
   \text{EBITA Interest Coverage Ratio} = \frac{\text{EBITA}}{\text{Interest Expense}}
   \]

   Plugging in the values:

   \[
   \text{EBITA Interest Coverage Ratio} = \frac{11,522}{169} \approx 68.04
   \]

Therefore, the EBITA Interest Coverage Ratio for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately **68.04**.

To determine the Return on Assets (ROA) for Costco Wholesale Corporation for the year ending September 1, 2024:

\[ \text{ROA} = \frac{\text{Net Income}}{\text{Average Total Assets}} \]

### Step 1: Identify Net Income for 2024
From the income statement:
- **Net income attributable to Costco** in 2024 is $7,367 million.

### Step 2: Calculate Average Total Assets
Total assets are given at the end of each year:

- **Total assets as of September 1, 2024:** $69,831 million
- **Total assets as of September 3, 2023:** $68,994 million

\[ \text{Average Total Assets} = \frac{\text{Total Assets (2024)} + \text{Total Assets (2023)}}{2} \]
\[ \text{Average Total Assets} = \frac{69,831 + 68,994}{2} \]
\[ \text{Average Total Assets} = \frac{138,825}{2} = 69,412.5 \text{ million dollars} \]

### Step 3: Calculate ROA
Using the values calculated:

\[ \text{ROA} = \frac{7,367}{69,412.5} \]
\[ \text{ROA} = 0.1061 \text{ or } 10.61\% \]

### Final Answer:
The Return on Assets (ROA) for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is **10.61%**.

To compute the UFCF (Unlevered Free Cash Flow) for Costco Wholesale Corporation for 2024, we need to follow these steps:

1. **Calculate NOPAT (Net Operating Profit After Taxes):**
   - Start with Income Before Income Taxes: $9,740 million.
   - Adjust for taxes: Net Income = Income Before Income Taxes - Provision for Income Taxes = $9,740 - $2,373 = $7,367 million.

2. **Adjust NOPAT for Non-Cash Items (Depreciation and Amortization):**
   - Add Depreciation and Amortization: $2,237 million.
   - Adjusted NOPAT = Net Income + Depreciation and Amortization
     \[
     7,367 + 2,237 = 9,604 \text{ million}
     \]

3. **Calculate Changes in Working Capital:**
   - Identify the changes in current assets and liabilities:
     \[
     \Delta Current Assets (2024) = 34,246 - 35,879 = -1,633 \text{ million}
     \]
     \[
     \Delta Accounts Payable (2024) = 19,421 - 17,483 = 1,938 \text{ million}
     \]

   Working Capital Changes:
   \[
   ΔWorking\ Capital = ΔCurrent Assets + ΔAccounts\ Payable
   \]
   \[
   ΔWorking\ Capital = (-1,633) + 1,938 = 305 \text{ million}
   \]

4. **Calculate Net Capex (Capital Expenditures):**
   - From the cash flow statement:
     \[
     Additions\ to\ property\ and\ equipment = 4,710 \text{ million}
     \]
   
   There is no mention of proceeds from disposals or other adjustments for capital expenditures in the provided data. Therefore, we assume that Net Capex equals additions.

5. **Calculate UFCF:**
   - Formula:
     \[
     \text{UFCF} = \text{Adjusted NOPAT} + ΔWorking\ Capital - \text{Net Capex}
     \]
   
   Plugging in the values:
     \[
     9,604 + 305 - 4,710 = 5,200 \text{ million}
     \]

**Conclusion:**
The Unlevered Free Cash Flow (UFCF) for Costco Wholesale Corporation for 2024 is **$5,200 million**.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate

are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.

reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
